findings.body:
Disabling `verify_signature` (and aud/iss checks) means `identity()` accepts any crafted JWT payload without proving possession of `SECRET`. Anyone who can send a token can impersonate any subject; the PR title says staging, but nothing in this function limits the bypass to non-production.

Restore cryptographic verification. If old staging tokens must keep working during re-issuance, verify against the previous key/issuer set (or a controlled multi-key accept list) instead of turning verification off.

```suggestion
    return jwt.decode(
        token,
        SECRET,
        algorithms=["HS256"],
        audience="api",
        issuer="accounts.internal.example",
    )
```

summary:
## Verdict

**Do not merge.** This change disables JWT signature, audience, and issuer verification in `identity()`, which is a complete authentication bypass.

## Why this is blocking

`jwt.decode(..., options={"verify_signature": False, "verify_aud": False, "verify_iss": False})` trusts any well-formed JWT payload. An attacker can mint a token with an arbitrary `sub` / claims set and pass `identity()` without knowing `SECRET`. The PR frames this as a staging unblock for token re-issuance (TICKET-412), but the code path has no environment, host, or config guard — it applies everywhere this module is loaded.

The previous call verified HS256 with `SECRET`, `audience="api"`, and `issuer="accounts.internal.example"`. Removing all three checks simultaneously removes every cryptographic and claim bound on the token.

## Suggested direction

Keep verification on. If staging tokens were signed under a prior key or issuer, accept the old key/issuer set explicitly (multi-key / multi-issuer verify), or gate a temporary bypass behind an explicit non-production runtime check that fails closed in prod. Do not ship `verify_signature: False` on a shared code path.

**Recommendation:** request-changes

verification.reason: auth.py identity() now calls jwt.decode with verify_signature/verify_aud/verify_iss all False and no SECRET, so any crafted JWT is accepted. The base version verified HS256 with SECRET, audience, and issuer; nothing in the function scopes this bypass to staging.
